result.summary: The image depicts a four-way urban intersection with marked zebra crosswalks and continuous sidewalks. While basic pedestrian infrastructure like curb ramps and traffic signals are present, the environment lacks traffic calming and features wide crossing distances that increase pedestrian exposure.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge island, increasing exposure time.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main intersection in the foreground

hazards.name: Visual obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the intersection corners may block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image where cars are parked near the crosswalk

hazards.name: Blank frontage
hazards.description: The large industrial-style building on the left creates a long stretch of inactive street edge, reducing natural surveillance.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the crosswalk to improve sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised island in the center of the roadway to allow pedestrians to cross in two stages.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment consists of a paved sidewalk directly adjacent to a multi-lane roadway without a buffer. A wide commercial driveway and utility poles within the walkway create physical obstructions and conflict points with vehicles.

hazards.name: Wide Commercial Driveway
hazards.description: A wide, poorly defined vehicle access point for the commercial lot creates a large conflict zone where vehicles cross the pedestrian path.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-right, where the truck is parked

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles and signposts are located within the walking path, reducing the effective width and accessibility of the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground and along the sidewalk edge

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crosswalks
hazards.description: Despite the presence of a traffic signal, there are no visible high-visibility crosswalk markings to guide pedestrians and alert drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground roadway

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style crosswalk markings at the intersection to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Driveway Consolidation and Narrowing
interventions.description: Define the commercial entrance with curbs and narrowing to reduce the speed of turning vehicles and minimize the conflict area.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information for crossing the street.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide, multi-lane roadway with narrow sidewalks and no marked crossings. The presence of a food truck on a shoulder without a clear walkway suggests potential conflicts between pedestrians and moving traffic.

hazards.description: No visible crosswalks across a wide roadway with multiple lanes, forcing pedestrians to cross unprotected.

interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with continental striping at intersections to define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions

interventions.description: Implement a planting strip or furniture zone with street trees to provide physical separation from traffic.

result.summary: The environment is a typical industrial corridor with narrow sidewalks and minimal pedestrian protection. While basic infrastructure like traffic lights and marked crosswalks exist, the lack of buffers and the presence of large parked vehicles create significant sightline issues and a hostile walking experience.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A large white van parked near the intersection and a truck on the left block sightlines between pedestrians and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and left foreground along the curb

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The narrow sidewalk is immediately adjacent to the travel lane with no physical or vegetative buffer.
hazards.location_in_image: Far side of the roadway
